newsitem.title: HUNGARY: AGRANA REFUSES TO PAY MORE TO HUNGARY BEET GROWERS.
newsitem.headline: AGRANA REFUSES TO PAY MORE TO HUNGARY BEET GROWERS.

text.p: Hungary's biggest sugar refiner said on Monday it could not up the price it is to pay disgruntled beet growers for the 1997 crop.
"This is simply the best offer we can give," Zoltan Brath, vice-president of Agrana-controlled Magyar Cukor Rt, told Reuters.
Producers said on Monday the plants' offer of the equivalent price of 57.5 kilograms of sugar for a tonne of beet, or 44.9 percent of the expected 128 kilograms per tonne, was too low.
Austria's Agrana has an over 50 percent share of Hungary's refining capacity, with the rest divided between France's Eridania Beghin-Say and Britain's Tate & Lyle.
Brath said he was surprised by the producers' move as Magyar Cukor Rt expected to continue negotiations on Monday.
"We had a round of talks on Wednesday and producers said they would answer our proposal by Monday evening," he said.
Sugar beet producers went ahead of the Monday evening deadline by holding a news conference earlier today.

Brath confirmed that Hungary had some 100,000 tonnes sugar surplus that will have to be exported at a loss and said they would seek to sell it on their traditional market, the states of the former Soviet Union.
